Decode one Protocol Buffers message

Source: R/decode.R
proto_decode.Rd

Decodes the bytes of one message of type type into a named list, one element per field, by the field's name. upb decodes the whole message first; R values are built only from a message that decoded completely.

Usage

proto_decode(
  x,
  type,
  pool,
  int64 = c("double", "character", "integer64"),
  enums = c("factor", "integer", "character"),
  defaults = TRUE,
  unknown = c("drop", "keep"),
  bytes = c("raw", "base64"),
  max_size = zpb_limits$max_size,
  max_depth = zpb_limits$max_depth
)

Arguments

x

The serialised message: a raw vector, a path to a file, or a connection. A file or connection is read up to max_size bytes.

type

The message type's full name, such as "pkg.Message".

pool

A pool from proto_pool() holding type.

int64

How 64-bit integer fields become R values: "double" (values beyond 2^53 lose precision, with a zuproto_precision_loss warning), "character" (exact decimal strings) or "integer64" (bit64::integer64() vectors, exact for signed values; needs bit64). Under "integer64", -2^63 (bit64's NA) and uint64 values above 2^63 - 1 become NA with a zuproto_precision_loss warning.

enums

How enum fields become R values: "factor", "integer" (the numbers) or "character" (the names). A number the enum does not define is NA with a zuproto_unknown_enum warning, except as an integer.

defaults

Whether unset fields without presence take their defaults (TRUE) or are left out (FALSE).

unknown

"drop" to discard fields the type does not define, "keep" to keep their bytes in an attribute proto_unknown on the message (and on each nested message) holding them.

bytes

How bytes fields become R values: "raw" or "base64" (strings, as protobuf JSON writes them).

max_size

The largest input accepted, in bytes. upb's memory for the decode is also capped, at a multiple of the input's size that the message type sets: the most a message of that type could legitimately need.

max_depth

The deepest nesting accepted: how many levels of messages within messages, the top-level message being level 0. A message holding a message holding a message is depth 2. A map entry counts as a level too, as upb counts it, so a message reached through a map is two levels down. At most 1000, so that hostile input cannot exhaust the C stack.

Value

A named list. An int32-family value of -2^31 is NA, with a zuproto_precision_loss warning, since R reserves it for NA.

Protobuf to R

ProtobufR
double, floatdouble
int32, sint32, sfixed32integer
uint32, fixed32double, exact
int64, uint64, sint64, fixed64, sfixed64per int64
boollogical
stringcharacter, UTF-8
bytesraw, or per bytes
enumfactor with the enum's value names as levels, or per enums
messagenamed list
repeated scalarvector
repeated messagelist of lists
map<K, V>named vector or named list, sorted by key
oneofthe member that is set
extensionelement named by its full name in brackets, [pkg.ext]

Well-known types: Timestamp becomes POSIXct in UTC, rounded to the microsecond; Duration a difftime in seconds; a wrapper (Int32Value and the rest) its value; Struct a named list, Value its value (NULL for null) and ListValue a list, as in protobuf JSON; Any a list of type_url and value (the packed bytes); FieldMask a character vector of paths; Empty an empty list. Repeated Timestamp, Duration and wrapper fields become vectors.

A field that tracks presence (a message, a oneof member, a proto2 or proto3 optional field) is left out when it is not set. A field that does not track presence cannot be told apart from its default on the wire; with defaults = TRUE it takes its default (0, "", FALSE, the enum's first value, an empty vector), as other protobuf runtimes do; with defaults = FALSE it is left out when it holds its default.

Required fields are not checked: a proto2 required field missing from the input decodes like any unset field.

See also

zuproto-conditions for the errors it raises.

Examples

pool <- proto_pool()
# A Timestamp of 1.5 seconds after the epoch: field 1 = 1, field 2 = 5e8.
bytes <- as.raw(c(0x08, 0x01, 0x10, 0x80, 0xca, 0xb5, 0xee, 0x01))
proto_decode(bytes, "google.protobuf.Timestamp", pool)
#> [1] "1970-01-01 00:00:01 UTC"
proto_decode(as.raw(c(0x08, 0x2a)), "google.protobuf.Int32Value", pool)
#> [1] 42
